details.title: KOREA’S RIFT OPENS ON SEPTEMBER 18
details.tagline: South Korea is getting ready for Riftbound.
headings: From Nexus Nights to Competitive Play
paragraphs: It's official, Riftbound is coming to Korea. Mark your calendars; on September 18, 2026 Riftbound's Origins hits Korean shelves, bringing players new ways to play and hold their favorite champions. Few places have had a bigger impact on League of Legends than Korea, and now Korean players will get to impact Riftbound. As we bring the newest way to play in the League universe to Korea, we’re looking forward to building on the League of Legends legacy and making Riftbound feel truly at home here.

The Riftbound x T1 2025 Worlds Champion Collection was just one of our first steps as we launch Korean Riftbound, bringing the 2025 World Champions into Riftbound with their own champ selections and signatures. Now, having seen the response from players the world over, we’re even more excited about what's ahead.

To celebrate Riftbound’s launch in Korea, players are invited to exclusive Riftbound events in two different locations in Seoul: GenG GGX (September 18-23) and Yongsan IPark Dopamine Station, 3F (September 18-30), where they can learn to play Riftbound and purchase the full range of Korean Origins products (Origins booster packs, five-card Origins booster packs, Origins Champion Decks, and Proving Grounds). Players who visit one of these locations will also have a chance to win limited edition items that are only available during this time (while supplies last)!
We wanted to take a moment and share an update on what players should expect with its launch, and what the roadmap afterwards looks like. And that will just be the beginning.

The splash of our Riftbound x T1 2025 Worlds Champion Collection announcement was amazing to see, and we were thrilled by the positive reaction as the team got to see the T1 2025 Worlds Champion Signature Edition for themselves.
That same idea carries into our launch, where we’re teaming up with Chimchakman and Nucksal. As big fans of them ourselves, we felt this was a great way to introduce players to Riftbound.

We're just getting started; we know players would love to see some familiar faces from the LCK and YouTube get their hands on Riftbound, so keep an eye out for more from streamers and competitors soon.
So, what comes after Origins? Quite a bit!
Spiritforged is next, launching in Korea this December!

Launching a new language for Riftbound, when we are starting with Origins, means the set release cadence has to be a compromise between letting players experience each Riftbound set as it is released, and the competing need to be faster than the global four sets-a-year cadence, so that they can eventually catch up with the global timing. Our goal is to bring Korean Riftbound in line with the global release schedule by the start of 2028 with Riftbound’s tenth set, meaning we will launch seven Riftbound sets in Korea during 2027, from Unleashed (Set 3) up to the unnamed Set 9.
The T1 Player Bundle will also be available in Korea later this year, matching the timing in the rest of the world. We'll have more information in the future, so stay tuned!
Before we get to Spiritforged and more, if you’re brand new to Riftbound with Origins launching, then there are several products you should look for to start your journey into the game:

Launching in Korean, Proving Grounds is a four-player box that comes with four complete Riftbound decks ready to be played out of the box. Meaning you and three friends are able to play with this single purchase!
Jinx, Lee Sin, and Viktor Origins Champion Decks
Origins includes three Champion decks, featuring Jinx, Lee Sin, and Viktor. Each of these are complete decks, ready to be played immediately.

We wanted to mark Riftbound’s arrival in Korea with a few special surprises that we knew we could only do here: two promos available through Korean launch events, plus a new Overnumber Ahri that can be found exclusively in Korean Origins packs.
Players have already spotted this version of Jinx, Demolitionist at MSI + Wildfest at our Riftbound booth. It features her original art with a special launch stamp to mark the occasion.

Also first appearing at MSI + Wild Fest, this version of Yasuo, Remorseful features brand-new art from South Korean artist Kim Star. Our art team was drawn to Kim’s work and the Korean cultural influences found throughout their style that felt truly tailored to launch.
Yasuo will also be exclusively available at select Origins launch events in Korea, though you may have to look a little harder to find him than Jinx.

Korean Origins booster packs will feature a new Overnumber Ahri, Nine-Tailed Fox, created especially for Riftbound’s launch in Korea. This version will appear alongside the original Ahri Overnumber in Korean Origins packs.

The artwork features a nod to Dynasty Ahri and was created by Allen Song, a Korean art director for Riftbound. Ahri herself debuted alongside League’s arrival in Korea, and we couldn’t think of a better champion to make a special card for.
We don't plan to introduce Korean-exclusive cards in boosters often, but this one seemed like the perfect celebration of League history for Riftbound's arrival.

With Riftbound launching in Korea for the first time while much of the world is up to Radiance, we want players in Korea to enter the Rift on a level playing field, with a community experiencing the same releases and same shared information.

That’s why we’re introducing Korean Standard alongside the release cadence; a temporary constructed format where the available card pool will grow alongside Riftbound’s Korean releases. This means events in South Korea will be, by default, using the Korean Standard format. This format is defined by the sets which have been released in Korean.

Imagine showing up to your first Nexus Night with a modified Origins Lee Sin Champion Deck and sitting across from a fully tuned deck built from cards released before Riftbound was even available in Korean. Not exactly the welcome we have in mind.
Instead, with the Korean Standard format, everyone starts with Origins and experiences each set together on the level playing field.

When Riftbound launches on September 18, Korean Standard will include cards from Origins. When Spiritforged arrives in December, it expands to Origins + Spiritforged. From there, the card pool will continue to grow with each Korean set release until global parity is achieved. This means this format is temporary by design.
The goal is simple: give the Korean community time to experience each set and build their collections, while steadily catching up with Riftbound players around the globe.
The global banned list will still apply to the Korean Standard format, so any cards on it are banned in Korean Standard.

Additionally, this is meant to be the default option in the region until we reach global parity. But players and stores can opt to play using the global Standard format, if they want. We just believe that having the Korean Standard format as default will help the community as it grows.

One of the great things about TCGs is that all you need to play are two people, two decks, and a place to sit. As we thought about Riftbound in Korea, we wanted to meet players in the places they already are.

Local game stores are a huge part of that and will remain a core element of Riftbound in Korea. But in Korea, we also knew we wanted Riftbound to be in PC bangs; places that have long been part of how League players meet, play, and spend time together, as well as a core part of creating experiences for Korean players.

We’re working with PC bang operators, including some of our longtime favorites and partners such as Gen.G GGX. Their PC bang will be a flagship and feature a dedicated Riftbound area and play opportunities.

We know not every PC bang has the same footprint, and we don’t expect Riftbound to look the same in each one. For some, it might be as simple as being able to grab some Riftbound packs to crack between games; for others, you might find dedicated gaming tables, events, and a full place to play.
We’re excited to see what Korean players make of Riftbound and how communities take shape across PC bangs, local game stores, events, and more.
From Nexus Nights to Competitive Play

Given the Korean release cadence, we’re also building an Organized Play experience specifically for Riftbound in Korea so we can ensure there will be places to play and competitive play that feels meaningful and exciting.

Nexus Nights will be the starting point: our weekly program where you can learn, meet other players, bring a deck, play some games, join your local Riftbound community, and maybe even get a Korean GG EZ Teemo.

For players looking for something more competitive, while Korean Riftbound catches up to the global set schedule, we’re building a unique Korean competitive pathway for 2027 that starts this December! This is the first event of a touring series for Korean players which continues through 2027.

We’ll have much more to share about Organized Play plans soon! Details on where to buy Korean Riftbound, pricing, and participating locations will also be shared through official channels ahead of September 18.
You can visit PlayRiftbound.com anytime to find upcoming Riftbound events near you.
We’re incredibly excited to be launching Riftbound in South Korea. Be sure to follow @RiftboundKR to stay up to date about what’s happening.

details.tagline: Ornn beat the heat to come out on top in Spain!
paragraphs: After a long hiatus, competitive Riftbound returned in a big way with over 2,130 competitors battling it out on Saturday, and 379 continuing the fight on Sunday. Of keen interest was to see what the Best-Of rotation would do to the field and while it definitely impacted some deck choices, others held the course with an eye to a top finish to earn a spot to one of the Regional Championships.

Pour one out for Ahri, Darius, Garen, Jinx, Lee Sin, Leona, Volibear, and Yasuo who were all missing from the main event. However, shout outs go to the Master Yi, Wuju Bladesman, Vi, Kai’Sa, Lux, Vikor, and Annie players who came to play. And a special nod to the lone pilots for Miss Fortune, Sett, and Teemo - we salute you.

The Top 8 featured five legends with the most surprising of them going on to win it all. MICE TheManLand took Ornn to victory, defeating CTCG Koko Lopez playing perhaps the deck of the event: Kennen. Kennen held three of the Top 8 slots, with Master Yi, Wuju Bladesman holding two, and the rest of the Top 8 was Ornn, our previous European RQ champion MICE Squirtle running back Azir, and Rengar being piloted by the dominant DSG Prismaticism.
The colored cells below reflect which decks were not competing for Best-Of.
Legend	# Played	% of Field	# Played	% of Field

Before we get to the decks, we want to clarify the naming of Best-Of cards. As Riftbound grows we’re going to find, from time to time, a need to realign on terminology. Best-Of prizing has reached one of those cases.

Up to now ‘Best-of’ has been used interchangeably as the naming of when someone is #1 with their Legend in a tournament, as well as for the prize received for doing so. When it was just Regional Qualifiers offering those prizes it wasn’t an issue. But now that Showdown Series are underway and more and more players are attending those events (703 at NRG Milwaukee this past weekend!) We need to refine the terminology as a Showdown Series Best-Of prize is not the same as a Regional Qualifier Best-Of prize (which is also not the same as what will be awarded at Regional Championships.)
So, we feel the need to divorce the term Best-Of from being both the finish and the award, and be more specific on what the prize being given is:
Best-Of - The achievement of being #1 with your Legend at a tournament.
Foil Plated Legend - The award received for being a Best-Of at a Regional Qualifier (or a Riftbound Regional next year.)
Foil Overnumber Plated Legend - The award received for being a Best-Of at the upcoming Regional Championships.
Plated Legend (or Non-Foil Plated Legend) - The prize awarded at Showdown Series events, and are also available on the Prize Wall at Regional Qualifier events.

We know that many players will continue to use the confusing ‘Best-Of’ as a shorthand for the prizes awarded, but we are asking the community, organizers, and other entities who track or list these for various purposes, to adopt this nomenclature.

articles.title: Vendetta Rules FAQ and Clarifications
articles.summary: Answers for some frequent questions regarding Vendetta’s core rules update.

details.title: VENDETTA RULES FAQ AND CLARIFICATIONS
details.tagline: Answers for some frequent questions regarding Vendetta’s core rules update.
paragraphs: Welcome to the FAQ for our first worldwide set release, the Vendetta FAQ! These are questions we’ve gathered from public discussion, from judges across the world, and from members of our own team. We appreciate everyone’s excitement and energy as they discussed the rules update for Vendetta; we hope this FAQ will clarify some points that may have been unclear, or provide answers to common questions you may run into.

One point we want to address directly: as we transition to worldwide release, our FAQs have a delicate timing. We want to gather as many real questions from players and judges as possible, while ensuring players aren’t left in the dark for too long on points that are confusing from the new set. If we release the FAQ too early, we might not catch the things that players are finding confusing; while if we release it too late, players can’t use it to prepare themselves and their decks for upcoming events. For future sets, we’re looking to try different models that might reduce some of the pain points players are feeling with this timing, but for now, we appreciate your patience.

The FAQ is a collection of official rulings. In places where the FAQ differs from the Core Rules Document, the FAQ takes precedence. When a new Core Rules Document is released, it will take precedence over any points that differ from this document.
Throughout this document, we use some specific shorthand to represent symbols in card text. Here’s a short guide:
[C] means “one power of this card’s domain”
[C] in Accelerate costs takes on the domain of the Unit, or turns into [A] if the Unit has no domain or multiple domains.
[C] in other cases is treated as the corresponding power symbol in all respects, matching how the cards are actually printed—it’s just a design shorthand!
What happens when you play Abandon on a spell that was played for its Flow cost?
It will be banished when it attempts to leave the chain.

“[T]hen banish it” in flow’s text is short for “if it would leave the chain after becoming a finalized chain item, and leaving the chain wasn’t instructed by its own execution, banish it instead.” Abandon returns the countered card to hand after countering it, but for the purposes of flow’s “then banish it”, this is also leaving the chain. No matter how it happens, as long as the flow spell leaving the chain wasn’t instructed by the execution of the spell itself, it will be banished.
This also applies to effects like Kai’Sa, Evolutionary from Origins, or Fizz, Trickster from Spiritforged.
What is the difference between Iascylla and Azir, Sovereign’s uses of “this battlefield”?
Iascylla’s delayed trigger refers to the battlefield that she held. Azir, Sovereign’s attack trigger refers to the battlefield where he is located.

The difference between these two is that Iascylla has a delayed trigger that references implicit information from her trigger condition: the battlefield where she held. Azir, Sovereign’s attack trigger does not reference information from his trigger condition, which purely checks for the event of Azir gaining the attacker designation for the first time each combat. Without that information being checked from the trigger condition, the “this battlefield” in Azir, Sovereign’s attack trigger will be checked when the triggered ability resolves. If it resolves and he is not located at a battlefield, any instructions related to that battlefield will be ignored; otherwise, the battlefield he is currently located at will be used.

Comparatively, when a triggered ability refers to information from its trigger condition, that information is checked when the ability triggers and not on resolution. In the case of Iascylla, her delayed trigger is linked with her hold effect, so the information from the trigger condition of the hold effect can be shared with the delayed trigger.
In future sets, we’ve moved to use more precise templating and wording for abilities like Iascylla’s.
What happens when I play Moonfall choosing an enemy unit while I control an empowered Mel, Newly Awakened?
The chosen unit will be given -3 [M]. All other enemy units at the chosen battlefield will be given -2 [M].

Mel, Newly Awakened’s empowered ability is a replacement effect. It replaces the event of a spell or ability you control giving a unit it chooses -[M]. The event it replaces that with is the spell or ability giving an additional -1 [M].

Although Moonfall gives -[M] to multiple units, only one of them is chosen, and thus the only event that is eligible to be replaced is the chosen unit being given -2 [M]. It will be replaced with that unit being given -3 [M]. The events of the other units being given -[M] will not be affected by this replacement effect.
What about casting Stupefy while I have an empowered Mel, Newly Awakened?
The chosen unit will be given -2 [M], to a minimum of 1 [M]. If it was 2 [M], it will become 1 [M].

In the case of Stupefy, Mel, Newly Awakened replaces the event of Stupefy giving -1 [M] with it giving -2 [M] instead. However, a replacement effect that replaces an event modified by the game effect that generated that event will inherit any of those modifications. In this case, Stupefy modifies the “give -1 [M]” game action and thus event with “to a minimum of 1 [M].” The replaced event will inherit the same modification.
Speaking of Mel, can my opponent play Abandon on my spell while I control an empowered Mel, Newly Awakened? What happens?
They can play Abandon targeting your spell. On resolution, they will Predict, but nothing else will happen.

Mel, Newly Awakened says “your spells and abilities can’t be countered.” If the spell can’t be countered, Abandon will attempt to counter it and fail, and then it will replace the event of it being put in the Trash with it being returned to its owner’s hand. However, that event never occurred, so there is nothing for the replacement effect to replace. Thus, Abandon will resolve to no effect. The replacement effect only functions within the limit of the resolution of the ability (it’s not a delayed replacement effect that specifies a duration), so even if the spell resolves later, it will go to the Trash as normal.
How does it work if I cast Abandon while having an empowered Mel, Newly Awakened but they Rebuttal my spell?

In the case of Rebuttal, gaining control of a spell is not the same thing as countering that spell. Effects that prevent spells being countered don’t prevent their controller from changing. If Rebuttal is played choosing your spell, and they pay [A] during resolution of Rebuttal, they will gain control of it. However, them not paying [A] does not mean the spell will be countered.
What new choices can I make when I play Rebuttal and pay [A]?
You can choose any number of targets or modes to make new choices for. The rest remain the same.

If you are remaking choices in this way, any choices you choose not to remake must be legal choices. You can’t choose to have some but not all choices be legal choices. Of course, you can always choose not to make new choices. In that case, any of the current choices will remain in their current state, whether that state is illegal or not.

If a spell has some rules or requirements about the choices made for it, those apply regardless of who controls that spell. For example, if a player plays a spell from face down, they must target game objects located at the battlefield the spell was played from unless the instructions of that spell indicate that a target must be chosen from some other location. Gaining control of such a spell doesn’t change this requirement when making new choices for the spell.
We’ll look at shaping up this section in a future rules update.
What happens if I choose to copy an empowered unit when I equip an unempowered unit with Shady Spectacles?
Being empowered is a status and is not copyable, thus the equipped unit will remain unempowered.

Shady Spectacles applies a copy effect to the equipped unit. Copy effects copy the printed (or copied, if another copy effect has already been applied) traits of the unit being copied. empowered is a status, a temporary modification, and not part of the printed traits of the card, so it will not be copied by Shady Spectacles. Whatever temporary modifications are applied to the unit as the copy effect is executed on that unit will be unaffected by the copy effect. If the unit has Might increases or decreases, a buff, the empowered status, Temporary, attacker, defender, etc those will remain in place.
What happens when my opponent’s Akshan, Mischievous steals my equipped Shady Spectacles? What happens if they want to copy Aphelios?

If it was attached to a unit, the equipped unit loses its copy effect. Akshan will then become a copy of a friendly unit of his controller’s choice. If he becomes a copy of Aphelios, his ability will not trigger.

This question deserves a bit more depth. As of the Vendetta rules update, we have clarified how effects like Shady Spectacles and Svellsongur work; they are replacement effects that replace the event of the equipment being attached to a unit with that event plus whatever their effect specifies.
In the case of Svellsongur, the resulting series of events will be:
Attach → Copy the equipped unit’s text to Svellsongur’s effect text for as long as Svellsongur is attached
For Shady Spectacles, the resulting series of events will be:
Attach → Choose a friendly unit and make the equipped unit a copy of that unit for as long as Shady Spectacles is attached

These events are not simultaneous. The attach event executes first, and then whatever event is instructed by the replacement effect is executed. Thus, the answer in the Spiritforged FAQ is no longer true: if you attach Svellsongur to Aphelios, he will not trigger twice. Svellsongur doesn’t have the copied effect text when the attach event executes.

Similarly here, if Akshan nabs Shady Spectacles from an opponent, it will attach and then make him a copy. If his controller chooses to make him a copy of Aphelios, it’s too late by that point for his new triggered ability to see the attachment event; it’s already been completed.

My Sand Soldier has Shady Spectacles equipped and is a copy of Azir, Ascendent. What happens if I activate the copied Azir’s activatedability before detaching the Shady Spectacles and then attach them to the same Sand Soldier as a copy of the same Azir, Ascendent? Can I use the activated ability again?

Each instance of the copied ability is a different ability. The game object remains the same throughout this whole process, so any temporary modifications will remain on the Sand Soldier as it transforms, but the copied rules text is an entirely new instance of the ability. It is the same idea as Svellsongur’s copy of an ability being “refreshed” if Svellsongur is detached and then reattached to the same unit.
What happens during combat damage assignment if my 4 [M] unit has both Ki Barrier and Lotus Trap played on it this turn and my opponent has a 4 [M] defender?

You can order the replacement effects on your unit. If Ki Barrier is first, your unit will take no damage and you will have 3 damage prevention remaining on your unit. If Lotus Trap is first, your unit will take 1 damage and will have no damage prevention remaining on your unit.

With the Vendetta rules update, we’ve streamlined how replacement effects that apply to damage work in combat. Specifically, any replacement effect that would apply to combat damage being dealt will apply instead to combat damage assignment. This was already the case for prevention effects like Ki Barrier or Counterstrike, to prevent several strange edge cases. Now, damage increasing replacement effects will also apply during damage assignment.
What happens when I discard a Patched Porobot with Hwei, Brooding Painter’s move trigger?
Two triggers will go on the chain, in the order of your choosing. One says “Give me +3 [M] this turn.” while the other says “Ready up to 2 runes.”

Hwei, Brooding Painter says “do the following based on the discarded card's type …” Unlike our previous reflexive triggers printed on cards that use a similar template (cf Twisted Fate, Gambler), Hwei doesn’t say “do one of the following …” As long as the card has the appropriate type, you will put the corresponding reflexive trigger on the chain. If somehow there existed a card that was a spell unit gear, you would put three reflexive triggers on the chain when you discard it to Hwei.
If my opponent plays two spells in succession, can I counter the first one with Crumbling Sands?

Crumbling Sands uses the “finalize” meaning of play, because it checks whether cards have been “played” and isn’t a triggered ability. As long as an opponent (not even necessarily the one who played this spell) has chosen targets, paid costs, checked legality, and completed the process of finalizing another spell, even if that spell was countered, Crumbling Sands can counter a spell. That means it can counter the first spell played, as long as another spell was played by an opponent after that one.
When can I react to my opponent playing Fallen Feline to a battlefield? And how does naming a card work?
You can react to the play effect of Fallen Feline, before they’ve named a spell.

Fallen Feline’s play effect instructs its controller to name a spell. This occurs on resolution of the triggered ability. If Fallen Feline is played to a battlefield, as soon as the ability resolves, opponents cannot play spells with that name. Meaning spells by that name can not be put onto a chain. Any spells already on the chain when Fallen Feline’s ability resolves will be unaffected. However, by the time you know the chosen spell it’s too late to play that spell.

Naming a card or tag has new rules with the Vendetta rules update. When naming something in this way, the overarching rule that applies to all naming is that you can’t name something that doesn’t exist in Riftbound. You can’t name the “Locke” tag, the “totem” type, nor a card named “Lingering Tentacles,” because none of those has been printed on cards or tokens in Riftbound.

However, you can name a card using information that uniquely identifies it. That information could be its name, but it could just as well be something like “the [3] spell with Flow that makes tentacles” or “the red Kai’Sa” or “Illaoi.” As long as there is no ambiguity as to what card is being named, a player can use whatever method is clear to their opponents and teammates. You can’t name a card by saying just “Kai’Sa” if there are two or more cards that could be identified in that way—you won’t have named a card if that’s all you say.
If I disempower a Kayle, Justified who has been empowered 3 times, does she lose all of her empowered statuses?
No. She will lose one of her empowered statuses.

For every Riftbound card other than Kayle, empowered is a binary status. They are either empowered or not. Kayle utilizes the golden rule “Card text supersedes rules text” to overcome this and be able to escape the normal bounds of what the empowered status means. On Kayle, empowered isn’t a binary status but a stacking status; she can have up to 3 empowered statuses. When Kayle is disempowered, the disempower action attempts to remove the empowered status. If she only has one empowered status, great, it’s gone. If she has more than one empowered status, the disempower action will remove one of the empowered statuses from Kayle.
But can I activate Kayle’s empower ability even if she’s already empowered?

Kayle’s empower ability can be activated any number of times. If she has less than 3 empowered statuses, she will become empowered. If she has 3 empowered statuses, the ability can still be activated but nothing will happen when the ability resolves.
What happens if my opponent plays Flash on their Akali, Silent that’s currently in combat after I play Star-Crossed targeting her?
Akali will be unaffected by Star Crossed as it resolves.

Akali, Silent is what the rules refer to as “untargetable” for enemy spells and abilities when she isn’t in combat; meaning she is not a legal target for them. Enemy spells and abilities being played when she’s untargetable can’t choose her. If she becomes untargetable after she’s already been chosen by an effect and retains it as that effect begins to resolve, it will “mistarget” her. She will be unaffected by any of the spell or ability’s instructions. If an instruction chooses only her, that instruction will be ignored.

I have a Ravenbloom Student on the board and I haven’t played any spells this turn. What happens when I play Rebuttal targeting my opponent’s Stupefy and pay [A] on resolution? After everything resolves, how much will Battering Ram cost? Will my opponent’s Legion abilities be active?
Ravenbloom Student will trigger twice, Battering Ram will cost [4], and your opponent’s Legion abilities will be active.

Ravenbloom Student’s triggered ability checks whether a spell that you control resolves. You gained control of the Stupefy, and it resolved, so you will have triggered Ravenbloom Student’s ability. Battering Ram and Legion, on the other hand, check whether cards were finalized. Although you gained control of Stupefy, you did not finalize it; you got it after it was already finalized by your opponent. Thus, your opponent’s Legion abilities will be active, and Battering Ram will only receive a [1] Energy discount.
What happens when I conquer with Swain, Visionary, if I’ve only played a Patched Porobot and Stupefy this turn?
You will score 2 points total. 1 from conquering, 1 from Swain.

Swain only checks whether you’ve played a non-token unit, a non-token gear, and a spell. Checks like that do not care whether they were satisfied by multiple cards or a single card relevant to the trigger conditions.
What happens when my opponent plays Switcheroo on their 2 [M] unit and my empowered Gangplank, Naval?
Gangplank, Naval will replace his Might being lowered with him being given +3 [M] this turn.

Swap calculates the difference in Might and generates two effects: an increase, and a decrease. When a swap effect is applied to two units’ Mights, it gives those units +[M] and -[M] respective to who has the higher Might.

Under the hood, Gangplank’s replacement effect sees the event of him being given -[M] and replaces it with him being given +3 [M] this turn instead. The event of the other unit being given +[M] is unaffected by Gangplank’s replacement effect. By the time we apply the replacement effect, the difference between the two units has been calculated. In the example with the 2 [M] unit, the final Mights of the two units will be 2 [M] → 6 [M], and 6 [M] → 9 [M].
The way this works is not immediately obvious based on how the swap game action rules are written. We will clarify this in a future rules update.
Note that this logic also applies to Mel, Newly Awakened and Switcheroo.

What happens when my empowered Gangplank, Naval is moved by my opponent’s Blast Cone’s play effect and they exhaust Blast Cone to stun Gangplank? Will he be stunned? What happens if I then play Back Off choosing my Gangplank? Will he get +3 [M] this turn?
Blast Cone will stun Gangplank. If you play Back Off choosing your stunned Gangplank, he will not receive +3 [M] this turn.

Blast Cone’s triggered ability that stuns units doesn’t choose them, so Gangplank’s replacement effect can’t apply to that event. Back Off played on a stunned Gangplank does not actually perform the stun game action, because Gangplank is already stunned. It’s legal to play Back Off, but the instruction will be negated. In order for Gangplank’s replacement effect to replace an event of him being stunned, the stun game action must actually be performed. Similarly, if an effect that said “Friendly units can’t be stunned” were active with a friendly empowered Gangplank, Naval is on the board, a stun effect that is played choosing Gangplank wouldn’t generate an event that Gangplank could replace, because no stun game action is performed.
What happens if I play Stupefy on my 1 [M] empowered Gangplank, Naval? Will he get +3 [M] this turn?

In order for his replacement effect to apply, the event of him being given -[M] must occur. In the case of Stupefy played on a 1 [M] unit, no -[M] is given; it is snapshot to -0 [M]. Thus, there is no suitable event for Gangplank’s replacement effect to replace.
What happens when my opponent plays Hidden Blade targeting my Akali, Deadly Weapon in reaction to her move trigger? Will it still deal damage to the chosen unit?

Akali is another case where her ability refers to information implicit to its own trigger condition, similar to Iascylla. Akali’s “battlefield I moved to or from” doesn’t require her to be on the board in order for us to be able to identify it, nor does it reference information about her current state. Even if she leaves the board, that information was checked when her ability triggered, and it is still available to us on resolution.
Can I activate an empowered Heimerdinger, Inventor to ready 2 gear if my Jayce, Defender of Tomorrow legend isn’t empowered? What about if my Heimerdinger isn’t empowered?
You can activate Heimerdinger’s ability if he is empowered, regardless of the empowered status of Jayce, Defender of Tomorrow.
There is a bit of a trick here, in that there are two important details to this question relating to dependent keywords:

First is that a dependent keyword (the kind of ability that [Level][>] or [Empowered][>] are when they appear with the arrow) includes the whole of the ability, including the dependent ability. They’re all one object, so to speak.

Second is that a dependent keyword’s dependent ability still exists and can be referenced while it is inactive—that is, if its condition isn’t met. In this case, the condition is that the source of the ability is empowered.

Heimerdinger gains all activated abilities that have the [E] symbol in their cost, and he gains the entire ability, restrictions, costs, dependent keywords and all. In effect, Defender of Tomorrow’s ability that Heimerdinger is gaining is the whole line that says:
Heimerdinger can gain this ability even if Defender of Tomorrow isn’t empowered because of that second point we made previously.
The key rule for this case is 727.1.b.1., which reads:
The Dependent Ability is present on the card for the sake of reference or evaluation until the Condition is met.

This means that the ability isn’t active and its text isn’t being processed yet, but other effects can reference or evaluate its text before the condition is met. Heimerdinger, Inventor is exactly one such effect.
What card does Astral Heron’s triggered ability discount?
It discounts the next card played (added to the chain and queued for finalization) this turn after the ability resolves.
Astral Heron has received an erratum to update its wording: “When you play your first card each turn, if I'm at a battlefield, the next card you play this turn costs [2][A][A] less.”
What happens when I play Temporal Breach targeting my Elder Dragon in base and pay [A][A] for Dragon Roost while playing Elder Dragon? Will it be played to base or to Dragon Roost?
You can choose which of those two locations you want to play it to.

In general, there are not many cases where we have this kind of competing instruction: one effect that tells you to play a unit to one location, and one that tells you to play it to another. That being said, when they do arise with contradictory requirements, the precedent from other areas of the rules is that the player chooses one of those requirements and ignores all others.

Note that this only applies to mandatory positive requirements, ones that specify a location or method without also preventing the action from being performed to other locations or with other methods and that aren’t optional. For example, an effect like Perched Grimwyrm’s passive ability is a restriction on playing that unit to any location other than a battlefield you’ve conquered this turn. Rockfall Path’s passive ability is a restriction on playing units to Rockfall Path. If you’ve conquered only Rockfall Path this turn, you can’t play Perched Grimwyrm at all, because those two restrictions are contradictory.
In this case, the contradictory requirements don’t directly prohibit the playing of these units to other locations, so we can choose one of the contradictory requirements and ignore the rest.
What happens when I play Perched Grimwyrm while I haven’t conquered Dragon Roost this turn? Can I pay [A][A] and play it to Dragon Roost? What if I’ve conquered another battlefield this turn?

In Riftbound, “can’t” beats “can.” Perched Grimwyrm’s effect is a “can’t,” as in it can’t be played to any location but to a battlefield you’ve conquered this turn. Dragon Roost’s ability tries to give the Grimwyrm permission to be played to the Roost, but that can’t overcome Perched Grimwyrm’s own restriction. If you have no ability to play Perched Grimwyrm to Dragon Roost after paying for it, you will not be able to finalize Perched Grimwyrm at all. The actions taken as part of playing Perched Grimwyrm will be undone and it will be returned to the zone it was played from.

This is true even if you’ve conquered another battlefield this turn. If you have the ability, you can play Perched Grimwyrm to that battlefield without paying the additional cost of Dragon Roost, but you can’t play it to Dragon Roost itself unless you’ve conquered it.

Sharp eyed readers may remember that Baron Nashor doesn’t work this way. He enters at the Baron Pit regardless of effects preventing him from being played to battlefields. The reason for this is that Baron Nashor’s passive ability generates a delayed replacement effect, the one that reads “I enter there.” This replacement effect replaces the event of him entering to any other location with him entering to the Baron Pit. The replacement effect gets around effects like Mageseeker Warden which limit where you can play units. However, Dragon Roost is not written as a replacement effect. It tells you where to play the dragon you’ve paid the additional cost for, but it doesn’t specify how that dragon enters the board. Therefore it is a permission on play location, but not a replacement effect.
Can I disempower my Ambessa, Matriarch of War with Profiteer to empower my Kayle? Do I control my own legend?
Yes, you can disempower Ambessa, Matriarch of War with Profiteer. And yes, you control your own legend.
We don’t typically consider the possibility that any player controls a legend, because control of legends cannot change, but you do indeed control your own legend.

What happens if I play Dragon Form on a unit that has -1 [M] from Stupefy applied to it? Will my Fiora, Grand Duelist trigger? Is there a moment where my unit becomes 5 [M] before the -1 [M] from Stupefy brings it down to 4 [M]?

Although Dragon Form sets the base Might of a unit to 5 [M], it does so via layers. Layers are evaluated when the effect is applied and their evaluation includes all existing applied layer alterations. We process layers in order, starting from the Trait-Altering layer (where this base Might setting effect is applied), proceeding to the Ability-Altering layer (not part of this example), and proceeding to the Arithmetic layer (where Stupefy’s -1 [M] is applied), but this process happens instantaneously; there is no window while evaluating layers for the unit to see itself become 5 [M] and then go down to 4 [M]. As soon as the effect of Dragon Form is applied, the unit is 4 [M].
As a side note, Might is one of the traits that is managed in the Trait-Altering layer, and it is one of the copyable traits that copy effects can replace or add to.
What happens when I play Hostile Takeover gaining control of my opponent’s ready unit, move it to base, and then play Temporal Breach choosing it? Where will the unit go?
The unit will remain in Banishment.

Units cannot be played to a base of a player other than their own controller under any circumstances. Because the owner of the unit is the one being instructed to play the unit, and the location they are being instructed to play it to is a base other than their own, it isn’t possible to play the unit. During the check legality step of finalization, the unit will be returned to banishment from the chain and all actions taken will be undone.
My 11 Might Renekton, Brute is disempowered by my own Profiteer. What happens when my opponent plays Stupefy choosing him? Will his ability trigger? What happens if instead I activated his ability?
Renekton’s ability will not trigger in either scenario.

In order to “become 10 or more,” his Might would have to have previously been less than 10. “10 or more” is a state, and Renekton’s triggered ability checks for the event of him achieving that state. If he maintains that state, regardless of how his Might changes, he will not “become” that state.
What happens when I play Icathian Rain choosing a Recruit at Heisho, Shell of the World once and Irelia, Fervent in base five times? How many times do I pay for deflect?
You will not pay for deflect.

While your spell or ability chooses a unit at Heisho, Shell of the World, you ignore deflect while paying for the spell. Ignore, in this context, means you treat deflect on the specified units as being inactive, like it’s turned off temporarily. In the case of Heisho, it doesn’t specify any units whose deflect to ignore, so you ignore all instances of deflect on units.

This only applies to the specified spell or ability. You can’t play a spell or ability choosing a unit at Heisho, and then play another one choosing a unit at another location and not at Heisho and still ignore deflect. Only while at least one target of the spell or ability is a unit located at Heisho do you ignore deflect while paying costs for that spell or ability.
What happens when I play Hextech Ray on an Elder Dragon while Imperial Decree’s delayed trigger is active and I have an Immortal Phoenix in the Trash? Can I play Immortal Phoenix from the Trash?

Per the current rules, there is nothing that would stop Imperial Decree’s delayed trigger from triggering Immortal Phoenix. It is a triggered ability generated by a spell; it is attributed a kill action, and thus the spell that generated it will also be attributed the same kill action. The owner of Imperial Decree is the controller of the delayed triggered ability; the player responsible for the kill action is the one who controls the ability; and that same player is the owner of Immortal Phoenix in the Trash. Thus all three conditions for Immortal Phoenix triggering are complete, and it will trigger.
If I play Ride the Wind targeting my unit at Vilemaw’s Lair and attempt to move them to base, what happens?

This is a rules quirk that players and judges identified as a result of a small additional rule added in the Vendetta rules update. We’re going to give some clarity to this that will resolve this issue, but if you don’t understand the conversation or why it is necessary, don’t worry. This isn’t an actual change to how we’ve been interpreting and ruling cards, but smoothing out a bug.

In short, the linked instructions rules are too expansive currently on what qualifies as an “ignored” instruction. To clarify this definition: an ignored instruction is one that wasn’t performed as part of the execution of a spell or ability’s instructions because it mistargeted (i.e. because the targeted object wasn’t a legal target on resolution). This is a case where, for example, you play Hidden Blade choosing an enemy unit and they play Star-Crossed in reaction, returning their unit to hand. When Hidden Blade resolves, the unit isn’t on the board, so we ignore the “Its controller draws 2.” instruction. Alternatively, if Hidden Blade is given the Repeat keyword by the Academy and both executions target the same unit, this is the reason why the unit’s controller doesn’t draw 4 cards.

An instruction is not ignored if an ability, effect, or circumstance of the game prevents it from occurring. This could take the form of a replacement effect that replaces the event of the instruction with something else, it could take the form of an ability like Vilemaw’s Lair that says “Units can’t move from here to base.” or it could take the form of a game action like Buff or Ready being performed on a unit that already has the appropriate state. It could even take the form of a unit, gear, or spell no longer being in an appropriate zone as long as the instruction doesn’t target those objects. The instruction in these cases isn’t ignored, but instead negated. A negated instruction has its effects skipped, replaced, or prevented. A negated instruction will not cause any linked instructions to be ignored unless those instructions refer specifically to the action being performed.

If a unit at a battlefield says “I can’t be killed.” and a player plays Hidden Blade choosing that unit, the unit’s controller will still draw 2 on resolution of Hidden Blade. (The instruction was negated and not ignored, so the linked instruction will still execute.)

If a unit at a battlefield is chosen by Hidden Blade and in reaction its controller plays Flash moving it to base, that unit’s controller will not draw 2 on resolution of Hidden Blade. (The instruction was ignored, so any linked instructions will be ignored.)

If a unit at a battlefield is chosen by Hidden Blade and in reaction its controller plays Zhonya’s Hourglass, that unit’s controller will draw 2 on resolution of Hidden Blade. (The unit is on the board and can have its information checked, and the instruction was negated and not ignored.)

If a unit at a battlefield has been affected by Smite previously this turn and it is chosen by Hidden Blade, that unit’s controller will not draw 2 on resolution of Hidden Blade. (Although the instruction is executed, the unit is not on the board to have its information checked. Additionally, the unit was moved to a non-board zone by an effect other than Hidden Blade and thus no longer has a controller that Hidden Blade can reference.)

details.title: ALL EYES ON BARCELONA
details.tagline: Spain sees the first Vendetta Regional Qualifier kick off the new set’s competitive season.
paragraphs: Riftbounders are rising to the challenge in Barcelona for the next Regional Qualifier Barcelona at the Fira de Barcelona.

Competitors from all over the EU will come together from August 21-23 for a weekend packed with top-tier tournament play, community events, side attractions, various vendors, and rewards from the Prize Wall. Regional Qualifier Barcelona brings opportunities for Regional Championship invites, cash prizes and valuable Organized Play rewards, so don’t miss out on this exciting weekend.
There is something for every level of play at a Regional Qualifier, so here is everything you need to know before arriving in Barcelona.
All times in Central European Time (CET)
s/n Avinguda de la Reina Maria Cristina
Barcelona introduces Season 4 prizing with the release of Vendetta. This means even more exclusive rewards for players competing at the highest levels.

With a $25,000 prize pool on the line, competitors will battle for cash prizes, Regional Championship invitations, future RQ Competitor Passes, Prize Wall Tickets, exclusive event rewards, and more. The Regional Qualifier Champion will take home $6,000 as part of the event’s top prize.

Introduced earlier this season, the updated structure expanded rewards across the Top 128 and represents Riftbound Organized Play’s continued efforts to enhance the competitive experience for players at every stage of the tournament.
Full prizing details can be found below.
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top 128 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top 128 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top 128 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top 128 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top Cut Playmat
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Exclusive Art) – Top 128 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top Cut Playmat
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Alt Art) – Top 128 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Exclusive Art) – Top 8 Promo
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Exclusive Art) – Winners Playmat
• Jayce, Brilliant Inventor (Exclusive Art) – Winners Promo
Barcelona will feature 33 Best-Of Legends spanning Spiritforged, Unleashed, and the latest set, Vendetta.
Origins and Proving Grounds have ended as Best-Ofs and Plated Legends for Regional Qualifiers and will not be available in Barcelona.
Each Legend will have one Best-Of Legend awarded to the highest-placing competitor piloting that Legend, celebrating standout performances regardless of final placement.
Follow the action all weekend long on Riftbound’s YouTube and Twitch channels.
You can catch the action live starting at:
Our desk will feature Shai Burton, Amy Wosley, Joe Curley, and YamatoCannon.
Watch live on Riftbound’s YouTube and Twitch channels. Make sure you’re following so you don’t miss the opening match.
Following on the go? @RiftboundOP on X will have coverage throughout the weekend.
@RiftboundOP is also your year-round home for Riftbound Organized Play, covering everything from Nexus Nights and Summoner Skirmish Series to Regional Qualifiers, Championships, and Worlds.

Looking to add something special to your collection? The Secret Garden Bundle features exclusive alternate art cards, collectible accessories, and Unleashed booster packs, making it the perfect keepsake for fans of the set.

The Secret Garden Bundle will be available for purchase at Regional Qualifier Barcelona, Regional Qualifier Singapore, PAX West, Regional Qualifier Los Angeles, and additional events throughout the Vendetta season while supplies last.
Please note: At Regional Qualifier Barcelona, Secret Garden Bundles are limited to one per event badge, while supplies last.
Want to make sure you’re ready for Barcelona?

Visit the newly updated Rules Hub for the latest rules, regulations, and gameplay systems. Whether you’re double-checking interactions or reviewing tournament structure, this is your go-to resource heading into the weekend.
The anticipation is building to see which competitors will claim the coveted RC invites and who will stand above the rest and ultimately lift the trophy in Barcelona.
Barcelona represents another chance for competitors to make their mark before the next stage of Riftbound Organized Play begins.
Los Angeles, CA, USA: Los Angeles Convention Center, Sep 25-27, 2026

You can read more about Riftbound’s 2026 roadmap here. And if you missed Riftbound’s State of the Game last week, be sure to see the State of Play article which gave an overview for how our Organized Play programs are changing in 2027.
The Riot and UVS teams will be onsite throughout the weekend, so come say hello, share your feedback, and talk Riftbound with us.

Most importantly, thank you. Every Regional Qualifier has helped shape Riftbound Organized Play, and the passion, creativity, and competitive spirit of the community continue to make these events special. Whether we’ll see you in Barcelona, Singapore, Los Angeles, or at your local game store, we’re grateful to have you as part of the Riftbound community.

details.title: AUGUST MERCH STORE UPDATES
paragraphs: Hello Riftbounders, happy State of the Game week. We want to give a few updates about the Merch store and share details about the upcoming T1 2025 Worlds Champion Signature Edition drawing but we also want to share some exciting updates about the merch store.

We hinted at this in our June update but we couldn’t speak to it directly. We moved to a new warehouse partner for the Riot Merch store and we were thrilled to see the vast majority of players receiving their Vendetta orders on (or very shortly after) launch day! We are excited by what the new facility is enabling us to do when it comes to the Riot Merch store.

Now onto what many of you are here to learn about: We are very excited that the English version of T1 2025 Worlds Champion Signature Edition is coming up next week! This will coincide with a T1 event for the Korean versions happening on the same day, and the start of the process for our Chinese players as well.
Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9am Pacific - Drawing registration opens
Monday, August 17, 2026 at 6pm Pacific - Drawing registration closes
Thursday, August 20, 2026 - Emails for those selected in the drawing begin going out
Wednesday, September, 2, 2026 - T1 2025 Worlds Champion Signature Edition begins arriving for players

As noted above, we will do our first wave of drawings on Thursday, August 20. If needed, we will do a second wave on Friday, August 24, and then if also needed, a third email wave will begin Monday, August 27. We know this is an item players are excited about, so we will be sharing when these emails go out and when the drawing has officially concluded on our Riftbound X account.
There is no Catch Up pool for this drawing. Everyone who enters the drawing will have the same opportunity to be selected regardless of previous entries, purchases, etc.

This is a special product and we are taking additional steps to protect player orders. Riot and the warehouse will be using additional packaging on these orders to try and ensure they arrive in pristine condition to players.

Each serialized card in the T1 Signature Edition is one-of-a-kind, which means an identical replacement cannot be produced. If your product arrives damaged, you may return the complete T1 2025 Worlds Champion Signature Edition for a full refund.

details.title: RIFTBOUND’S CREATORS IN 2027
details.tagline: Updates and information for our creators as we head into 2027
paragraphs: Riftbound’s first year working with creators has been nothing short of inspiring. Meeting content creators from around the world and seeing them create such cool stuff for their respective communities has demonstrated that creators are invaluable in showing off all the different ways to love Riftbound. We’re incredibly grateful to work with such fun, creative, passionate gamers on a daily basis.

Riftbound’s first year (and first four sets) has already allowed us to work with hundreds of creators in lots of different ways. Riftbound creators revealed an incredible 213 cards around the globe. We worked with hundreds of creators across our set releases to create Riftbound content. We’ve even contracted creators to help us make some cool stuff for Riftbound’s own channels, like the Unleashed Dev Drop and our mechanics explainer videos.

A card game without someone to play it with isn’t nearly as much fun, and it's the community voices sharing Riftbound online that have helped make it such a wonderful place to be. In short, if you're making videos, posting about your Nexus Nights, cosplaying, or supporting anyone doing any of these things online, you’re what’s made Riftbound so great.

Looking ahead to 2027 our goals take this work one step further. We want to work with more individuals the world over as Riftbound continues to grow globally. We want to lean harder into support for specialized content such as high-level competitive play, super-niche collectibility, and more! To do this, we are working to create a clear and reliable process for creators to get involved in these initiatives.

As Riftbound is growing and we’re establishing how best to work with creators, we are not going to join the RPP yet. As always, we will see how things evolve and how Riftbound continues to grow. For now, Riftbound’s creator programming will continue to be handled set over set; our work is focused on improving the ways more creators can be seen and considered for us to highlight and have them get involved. We have trusted partners that we’ll continue to work with, but with every set we will bring new creators into the spotlight to share the excitement.

When a new set is announced, we will share a link for creators to apply to get involved. This link will be at the bottom of future set Overview articles, as well as shared elsewhere. Apply for the sets that resonate with you, and tell us what you’d like to make! You’ll be able to apply for every set, but there are no guarantees on being selected. Our goal here is to explore relationships with new creators and to grow together as a community.

As with previous sets, the partners who we work with during preview season will receive product to create content ahead of launch. That means that there’s even more reason to keep an eye on previews, as those creators will be giving you the inside scoop on cool cards and combos ahead of your Pre-Rift event.

We’ll also continue contracting creators on a case-by-case basis for specific content needs like mechanics explainers, event activations, and more. The truth of it is that these opportunities are rare, and always different. What we can state explicitly is that we will continue to partner with new faces who show off the best of the Riftbound community.

There are some very important roles that don’t necessarily fall under a YouTube category or a typical hashtag, however. Casters, Cosplayers, and Website Developers provide a great deal of value to the Riftbound ecosystem, and have a very different set of collaboration opportunities available to them than a typical streamer or YouTuber.

Website Developers will all still need to submit their creations through the proper Dev Rel review channels, but are welcome to apply to participate in preview seasons (hope you all saw the cool Vendetta reveal that Piltover Archive created).

Cosplayers and Casters can apply for consideration at RQs, RCs, and their 2027 implementations, using these respective links. These running applications will be a constant reference point for event organizers and will also be available at the bottom of the Roadmap Article.

With November comes Riftbound’s first Regional Championship! It’s exciting to hit this milestone in our Organized Play circuit, but it does mean some changes to how we work with creators on site at events.

Next year, with the exciting changes to the Organized Play structure, we will be shifting our focus for on-site influencer management to the new Riftbound Continentals. There will still be Regionals where we show up for on-site influencer management, such as organizing creator Pre-Rifts, or trying other new things out, but they will be the exception rather than the norm that they have been this year.

We’ll still provide badges to creators wanting to make content at Riftbound Regionals, and we’ll still give them opportunities to become part of the action with their own events like Trivia or Meet & Beats. You all are such a creative bunch, and we wouldn’t dream of standing in your way of sharing that with other fans. The truth of the matter is that you’re the ones who make those events so special.

Lots of people ask what we’re looking for with our partner opportunities. The easiest answer we can give is passion. If you’re making content that speaks to what you love about Riftbound, and you’re doing it consistently, you’re already doing the most important things you can.
As far as specific types of content:
Card games will always have room for deck techs and combo explainers.
Learn to play content will always have value in something as strategic and complex as Riftbound.
We’ll always want to hear cool collector stories or watch interviews with pro players.
Whatever you're making, it probably has an audience we want to feel welcome and supported.
Create with authenticity, be a positive member of the community, work with each other, and don’t be afraid to try something new!

We’re dedicated to identifying new Riftbound creators to grow with the game in 2027, and looking forward to seeing what you talented individuals create. The past year has given us a lot of ideas and energy to work with, and we’re going to put it to good use in the months ahead!

We’d like to extend a special thank you to a few creators who helped us drive excitement and share their love of Riftbound in 2026: 50kComics, ADCourtney, Alanzq, Amandine Bamaca, AnzidMTG, Bamboojelly, BullfrogTCG, BunnyMonster, CapitaoSerket, ChaiTCG, ChallengerTCG, Curley Cards, Dam, Dekkster, Drakos, El Templo del Poro, emenoacid, Frodan, fromthesoul, Garajeux, GoodTimeSociety, Grapplr, Into the Rift, IreneRAWR, jem, Jimmy Wong, Jubes, Katchouze, LotharHS, LS, Lua Stardust, LynofLegends, Maldhoud, Medic, Mega Mogwai, MegFerarri, MERC, Mimimalanders, Miss Jourdy, MrsChimChim, nack, Narutak, NickyBoi, nikkinami, OTP, Phokky, Piltover Archive, Plumsoju, Pob, Ramekiano, Rapsolo, Recycle2, RiannePlaysRiftbound, Riftbound Report, Riftbuddies, Riftlab, Runeboyz, Scarra, Sebbie, Silv4n, Skittyx, Skuffey, Snnuy, Solary, Spuzie, The Asian Avenger, The Blevins, Tolarian Community College, ToxickBunny, tronisbad, TSS, Turn ‘em Sideways, Voci Dal Rift, xNavalha, Zmain and so many more of you.
Creators wanting to submit interest to work with us for the release of Legacy can fill out this form

details.title: AUGUST 2026 STATE OF PLAY
details.tagline: We’ve got a bunch of updates and news about Organized Play for Riftbound in 2027
paragraphs: The 2026 Organized Play season is still underway. There are Regional Championships left to play, Riftbound Worlds invitations still to earn, and plenty of stories that haven't been written yet.
So, before we look ahead to next year, we want to say thank you.

Over the past year, you've made Riftbound a thriving global community. You've filled local game stores, traveled across regions to compete, introduced friends to the game, and shown us what Organized Play can become.

Everything we're announcing today has been shaped by this first year and the lessons we've learned together. Our goal is to make Riftbound the best trading card game for players in the world. Yesterday we shared updates and answered your questions about how we’re continuing to do that with the sets and products we make, but today is about how we’re working to do that through our play programs.
In 2027, Riftbound Organized Play goes bigger.
More ways to play. More opportunities to compete. More reasons to come together throughout the year.
2027 represents a year of evolution for Riftbound play. Here’s a high-level summary of what is changing:
We’re adding the new Nexus Cup program, a new monthly tournament at local game stores.
We are retiring Summoner Skirmish and introducing the Riftbound Challenge Series to act as the first rung of our competitive ladder.
Regional Qualifiers are becoming Riftbound Regionals, with more of them spread around the world and throughout the year.
Regional Championships are becoming Riftbound Continentals, which will be our cornerstone event of each set.

Summoner Skirmish has been trying to do two things: first, it was trying to be the local championship event for your store, and second, it was also meant to be the on-ramp of our competitive play program. The prizing for Summoner Skirmish includes a bye to our Regional Qualifiers. It was a great idea in theory, but we underestimated how popular these events and RQs would be. This misalignment means that many of the byes awarded have gone unused because players simply can’t make it to events to use them.

Given these issues, and understanding what we needed, we felt it was the right decision to retire the Skirmish events after Radiance, and introduce two new programs for local game stores: the Riftbound Challenge Series, and the Nexus Cup. They are aimed at serving the two different goals we outlined above. Challenge Series will be the on-ramp for competitive play, while Nexus Cup acts as a local event aimed at crowning a local champion without directly driving into our competitive structure. We’ll talk about both below.
Summoner Skirmish events will continue through Radiance, but they will not offer byes, and their prizing will be augmented instead.

We want to make clear, byes are not suddenly being made useless. If you earn a bye from a Vendetta Summoner Skirmish, or if you have byes which you have not yet used at an RQ, you have the following options of what to do with them:
You can still make use of your bye at a Regional Qualifier this year, as well as at a Riftbound Regional event through 2027. They will still be honored for redemption to receive a first round bye.
We are working on plans to offer a make good for players who have unused byes and we will share more about it in the future.
That was a lot, and we're excited to show you the structure of Organized Play for 2027, but we know this would be an important topic for players to understand.
One Community. More Ways to Play.
Every player comes to Riftbound for different reasons.

Some players are looking for a welcoming place to meet up each week, try a new deck, and celebrate every new set with their local community. Others are looking for tougher opponents, bigger tournaments, and the opportunity to compete on Riftbound's biggest stages.
The 2027 ecosystem is designed to support both experiences.
The First Step on Your Competitive Journey

The foot of our competitive ladder starts in the game store. The Challenge Series is the successor to our Summoner Skirmishes. As we looked at our play programs, we found Summoner Skirmish was trying to do two things: It was trying to be both the local championship and it was also meant to be the lowest rung of our competitive program. Additionally, offering byes as a prize hasn't worked out the way we hoped, given how popular the game has been since launch. Many of the byes awarded have gone unused because players simply can’t make it to events to use them.

Given these issues, and understanding what we needed, we felt it was the right decision to retire the Skirmish series and introduce two replacements: this new Challenge Series, and a new program called the Nexus Cup which you’ll hear more about later.
Rather than spreading competitive play across thousands of overlapping events, Challenge Series focuses those moments into a curated network of stores throughout the season.

One of the newest additions to Organized Play is going to grow in 2027. This year we saw thousands of players join these events, run by a myriad of organizers around the world. Expanding the Riftbound competitive footprint from New Zealand to Canada to Poland! And we’re expanding on it for 2027.

2027 will see more Showdown Series events, more tournament organizers, and more regions receiving them. If Challenge Series is where your competitive journey begins, Showdown Series is a great next step.

We’re streamlining the name of Regional Qualifiers to just Riftbound Regionals. These events will remain fun global events for regional communities to come together for, with side events, vendors, and more fun activities for all Riftbounders to come and enjoy.

They'll be held throughout every set (generally three to four per set). They are still the premier destination for players looking to test themselves against the best in their part of the world. Regionals will qualify players for future Continental events.

Where our schedule for 2026 has been uneven, next year will see a more consistent global cadence for players. This means players will have regular opportunities to compete closer to home throughout the season, and to create lasting memories and friendships from the first set of the year to the last.
And yes, Best-Of Metal Legend prizes will continue.

Riftbound Continentals will be held in four marquee destinations around the world each year. They'll bring together Riftbound's biggest names, the game's rising competitors, creators, and players for weekends built around the highest level of Riftbound play.
These are the successor to this year’s Regional Championships, though they will differ in a few important ways:
Rather than occurring at the end of the year, we will hold Continentals throughout the year with a Continental tied to each set in cities around the world.

Continentals are three-day events, with Day 1 being open entry as a qualifier for those who haven’t already qualified to the Saturday and Sunday event, meaning everyone has an opportunity to compete in the main event at the Continental.
And for those who don’t qualify for the main event or don’t want to, there will still be lots of side events, chances to meet creators and members of the Riftbound team throughout the weekends.
The season concludes at Riftbound World Championship, where the year's best competitors come together to crown a World Champion.
As Riftbound’s capstone event of 2027 and the peak of the Riftbound competitive ladder, we'll be back with more information about it in the future.
There’s a lot to be excited about for those of you who want to take down the best the game has to offer.
Competitive play isn't the only way to experience Riftbound.

Most Riftbound games aren't played on the Worlds stage or at Regional events. Many more games are played at the local game store. While most of our changes in 2027 are around our Premier competitive play, that doesn’t mean we aren’t looking at the local events and evaluating how we can continue to drive and improve for players who attend events at their LGS week after week.

Local Organized Play is how we are organizing the way you play near your home and in your town. It continues to grow through recurring in-store events designed to help communities gather, welcome new players, and celebrate every new Riftbound set together.

Be among the first to experience every new set before release. By our measures for attendance, sentiment, and the way the community has adopted these events, Pre-Rifts have been an undeniable success of our first year and we see no need to mess with these.

Following Pre-Rift, we’ve heard from you all that Nexus Nights have been a huge success. They are the heart of Local Organized Play, bringing players together every week to play, try their new decks, and build lasting friendships in the community.

New in 2027, Nexus Cups will be monthly celebrations of local organized play, giving communities another reason to regularly gather, celebrate, and create memorable moments together outside of the Premier Play Ladder. As we mentioned above regarding the Summoner Skirmish, we felt that there needed to be an event at a local level which enabled local competition without driving and incentivizing players to push hard to earn their way onto the competitive ladder.

Today’s overview is meant to introduce the community to how we’re envisioning the play programs changing. We debated whether to dive into this today or hold off until we can provide the complete picture with the events, how players will qualify and progress through the premier play events, and a calendar of actual events.

We decided we didn’t want to let perfection be the enemy of the good by holding off sharing these updates until we had a fully locked in schedule. Our community has shown themselves to be smart and passionate, and we value our community and the trust and transparency we’ve built with them.

Some of you may have heard news that Riot’s working on a new platform to support our Organized Play program. Carde.io has been an integral partner in the launch and growth of Riftbound, and we're deeply appreciative of their unwavering support, collaboration, and belief in the game. This new platform is part of the next generation of organized play for the game.

Your local game store has been asked to begin the process of transitioning from Carde.io to the new platform, starting Sept. 14th, to the Riftbound Gaming Network platform. We expect stores to begin using the new Riftbound Gaming Network with Radiance events.

Our roadmap of work is such that the new platform will be up and running to handle all Riftbound events by the end of the year. We want to be clear, this program is going to launch and be in active development. We are not launching it and then moving on to other projects, there will be many features and improvements which follow in the weeks, months, and years to come. But we feel strongly that this is the right time to make this change and that it will offer a dedicated experience for players, with many benefits of sitting within the Riot ecosystem.

To try and ensure players have the best experience at events, we are going to keep Showdown Series events, which are managed by third-party tournament organizers, on Carde.io for the remainder of this year. However, we expect the European and North American Regional Championships to use PlayRiftbound.com.

Our goal remains to create the best and most exciting organized play program for our players. PlayRiftbound.com is a key step on that journey as we ease friction points and continue to improve the experience for our players. PlayRiftbound.com will be the one-stop home for Riftbound Organized Play, as the place where players will be able to sign up for events, see results, and more.
We'll have more information and updates about this platform in the coming months. Stay tuned!

Today’s article was about introducing you all to the structure and way we’re thinking about Organized Play as we head into 2027. We're still finalizing dates and locations with our partners around the world, and we'll share updates on the 2027 schedule with plenty of time for players to plan their travel.

Later this year we'll come back with a more detailed look at the new events, how players will progress through it beyond just direct qualifications, and also have some of next year’s dates so players can begin planning for 2027.
